SK2110 ToString() returns null

An override of object.ToString() returns a null constant on some path.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floor—
Since2.0
SupersedesS2225

Why

String interpolation, string.Concat, every structured logger and most of the BCL call ToString() and assume the result is a string. A null comes back as a NullReferenceException or a silently absent value somewhere else entirely, and the type that caused it is named nowhere in the stack. ⚠ The rule exists only where the compiler is silent, and that boundary was measured rather than assumed. A probe built with the .NET 10.0.400 SDK reports CS8603 on public override string ToString() { return null; } in a nullable-enabled context — so the rule declines there, because ADR-008's answer to a diagnostic the platform already ships is to use it. What the probe found the compiler saying nothing about is the other two shapes: public override string? ToString() => null;, which is legal and warning-free because object.ToString() is itself annotated as returning string?, and the same return null; under #nullable disable. Those are what this reports.

Example

Instead of:

public override string? ToString() => null;

Write:

public override string? ToString() => string.Empty;

When it does not fire

⚠ Constants only. The reported expression is one whose value the compiler already knows is null — a null literal, a default, or a cast of either. A ToString() that returns a variable which might be null is flow analysis, and in the two contexts this rule covers there is no flow state to read: under #nullable disable every expression's NullableFlowState is None, which is not MaybeNull and is not evidence of anything. Reporting on a guess there is how a rule acquires the false positives that get it switched off. ⚠ The nullable context does not silence this rule and that is deliberate, inverting the usual direction: #nullable disable is precisely where CS8603 is absent and so precisely where the rule is worth having. ⚠ Only overrides of `object.ToString()`. A ToString(string format) overload, an explicit IFormattable.ToString, and any unrelated method spelled ToString are left alone — their contracts are their own. ⚠ `return null;` inside a lambda or a local function nested in `ToString()` is not this method's return and is not reported. ⚠ The fix writes string.Empty and is fixIsSafe: false: it changes what the method returns, which is the point, but a caller that tests the result for null is relying on the bug and should see the change.
